title: Cross-Service Launch Sequencing and Timebox Allocation for Runtime/Console/API
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Objective: Define an operational sequencing plan and fixed timebox windows that let runtime, console, and API teams ship coordinated changes with predictable cutovers, minimal customer disruption, and clear rollback boundaries. Scope includes: sequencing rules, regional stagger timing, capacity guardrails for Dedicated pools, canary lanes for Console and API changes, escalation paths, and automated gating signals (SLO, error-rate, latency, cost anomalies). This ticket consolidates input from runtime, console, and API PMs and produces the deploy choreography, communication cadences, and the acceptance checklist for go/no-go decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Documented per-surface sequencing rules and timebox matrix agreed by all three PMs
Rollout playbook with canary lanes, blast-radius limits, and automated rollback triggers implemented in runbook
Capacity guardrail definitions for Dedicated and Hosted (min-reserve, burst-policy) codified and validated by infra team
A single cross-team cutover calendar in the shared calendar with owner, pre-cutover checklist link, and escalation contacts
Dry-run completed for one representative regional rollout with observed SLO telemetry and post-mortem notes
rollout_plan: 1) Preflight (T-10d): Freeze non-critical changes, run capacity sizing, and validate canary test prompts. 2) Canary (T-3d to T-1d): Deploy runtime canary to 1 region low-traffic pool; deploy Console and API feature flags to canary cohort; monitor SLOs and billing telemetry. 3) Regional Stagger (Cutover Day): Open 3-hour timebox per region in this order: EU -> NA -> APAC. Each region timebox: 30m deployment, 90m observation, 60m ramp. 4) Fallback windows: If error-rate > 2x baseline or latency P95 increases > 50% in observation, rollback runtime to previous model build and toggle API/Console flags off. 5) Post-cutover (T+1d): Collect metrics, run smoke tasks, capture session-level anomalies and write a short retro. 6) Full rollout gate: automated quality checks + PM sign-off required to proceed beyond initial regions.

Console owner: Mateo Alvarez - responsible for feature-flag rollback and UI revert steps

SRE lead: Jordan Price - executes capacity guardrail changes and monitors infra alarms
Escalation channel: #cutover-alerts (Slack) + PagerDuty for SEV escalation
risks: Runtime kernel incompatibility with new quantized weights leading to tail latency spikes
Capacity overcommit in Dedicated pools causing degraded throughput during ramp
Inconsistent feature-flag behavior between Console and API that increases customer error surface
Regional network instability impacting canary metrics and causing false positives in rollback triggers
